overall: The AG found no Open Meeting Law violation on any of three allegations: the minutes were accurate, no executive session was required, and the missing certification forms were promptly refiled.

allegations.summary: Minutes of the January 29 meeting allegedly were inaccurate because they did not list a letter the chair referenced during the meeting as a document used.
allegations.key_passage: As such, we find that the letter was not “used” by the Committee and thus the Committee did not violate the Open Meeting Law by failing to list the letter in the minutes as a document used at the January 29 meeting.

allegations.summary: The committee allegedly should have met in executive session under Purpose 1 to discuss the reputation and character of an individual raised in a letter.
allegations.key_passage: The Committee did not violate the Open Meeting Law by failing to meet in executive session.

allegations.summary: Two committee members allegedly did not timely complete the Open Meeting Law certification form after re-election.
allegations.key_passage: We find that the Committee took prompt remedial action in response to this complaint where both Mr. Bonfatti and Mr. Morrison refiled their Open Meeting Law certification forms with the Town Clerk upon learning that such forms were missing; thus we find no violation of the Open Meeting Law.

note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
